title: Stable JSON param lightweight spec and error mapping
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, stable JSON parameter specification for runtime tool/function calls that supports streaming responses, partial validation, and clear, actionable error mapping for client SDKs. The spec must be lightweight so authors can write it by hand, and it must define a deterministic error code set for telemetry and automated remediations.
background: We currently accept a broad variety of tool parameter manifests. This leads to ambiguous runtime validation, inconsistent user-facing errors, and brittle fallbacks between hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments. Recent incidents highlighted confusion when a tool mismatch returned a 500-like error instead of a clear parameter rejection. We need a minimal spec that runtime and SDKs can rely on to produce consistent behavior and telemetry.
proposal: Introduce a 'JSON Param Light' (JPL) format: a small, opinionated subset of JSON Schema with explicit parameter kinds (string, int, float, enum, object, array), optional 'streamable' flag for schemas allowed in streaming tool payloads, and a small set of validation modifiers (required, min/max, pattern, item_type). Define a canonical error taxonomy (INVALID_TYPE, MISSING_REQUIRED, OUT_OF_RANGE, PATTERN_MISMATCH, DEPRECATED_PARAM, UNKNOWN_PARAM, PARTIAL_PARSE) and a mapping to HTTP gRPC semantics and SDK exceptions. Provide a compatibility shim that can translate common older manifests into JPL at deploy-time, emitting conversion warnings.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc (single page) describing JPL syntax and semantics merged to docs/runtime/schemas
Runtime implements JPL parser and validator with <5ms median validation latency on 99th percentile of our workloads
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) map canonical error codes to typed exceptions and include human-friendly messages
Compatibility shim converts at least 90% of existing tool manifests without loss of semantics and emits conversion warnings for edge cases
Telemetry emits one unified metric for param-validation failures with error_code label and sample prompt/context metadata
E2E test harness with 40 synthetic tool calls covering streaming/non-streaming, partial payloads, and error cases
technical_notes: JPL intentionally omits full JSON Schema features (no allOf/anyOf/oneOf, no conditional subschemas) to keep parsing streaming-friendly

streamable: true indicates validate-as-chunk where runtime will accept object fragments and resolve when complete; validator must support incremental parsing and return PARTIAL_PARSE when a chunk is syntactically valid but incomplete
Unknown parameters are tolerated by default but produce UNKNOWN_PARAM warnings; a strict mode can be configured per-route or via manifest flag
Deprecated fields should include 'deprecated_since' and runtime emits DEPRECATED_PARAM with guidance string referencing migration doc

Error taxonomy maps to stable machine codes plus short user_message and optional remediation_hint. Example: {code: 'INVALID_TYPE', user_message: 'parameter "timeout" must be an integer', remediation_hint: 'convert to integer or use "5s" format'}
Validators must emit a stable 'validation_signature' hash for telemetry to group related failures across releases
Compatibility shim will live in model-onboarding pipeline; conversions recorded in onboarding logs and surfaced as warnings in Console tooling
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize JPL spec and internal review with runtime/SDK/PM/Design
Week 1: Implement parser and validator in runtime behind a feature flag; add telemetry metrics and tracing spans
Week 2: Ship SDK changes to map error codes to exceptions and user messages; add quickstart samples
Week 3: Run compatibility shim on production manifest corpus, generate conversion report and fix top 10 edge cases
Week 4: Enable JPL enforcement for new tool manifests; gradual enforcement for existing manifests with warning-only mode for 2 weeks
Week 5: Full enforcement with error-level validation; monitor rollout SLOs and rollback plan ready
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Strict validation may break older clients. Mitigation: default to warning mode and provide migration tooling and a permissive compatibility shim
Risk: Streaming/partial validation complexity increases runtime CPU. Mitigation: implement incremental validation paths and benchmark; add a config knob to disable stream validation per-route
Risk: Error code design locks API surface. Mitigation: choose conservative, extensible codes and allow SDKs to add 'subcode' freeform field for vendor-specific signals
testing_plan: Unit tests for JPL parser/validator covering scalar, arrays, nested objects, enums, and streamable fragments
Property-based tests that fuzz manifests and payloads to ensure validator does not crash or deadlock
Integration tests with streaming runtime to validate PARTIAL_PARSE, incremental KV cache interaction, and latency impact
SDK tests that assert mapping of error codes to typed exceptions and preservation of remediation hints
documentation_needs: Single-page spec with examples and conversion rules
Migration guide for manifest authors (common patterns and pitfalls)
Console warning UI copy and links to remediation steps
Telemetry dashboard showing validation failures by error_code and route
